## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}(x_1,x_2,\ldots)\), \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\), and this submodule is an ideal. [source-2, lines 1310-1321]
- [source-backed] The map \(s_\lambda\mapsto s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)\) induces \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}/\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^W_+\mathbb Z[\mathbf x]^{W_J}\), and the surviving Schur classes are indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\). [source-2, lines 1321-1331]
- [proved] Writing \(q=n-r\), the excerpt yields
  \[
  I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\not\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,\qquad
  \Lambda/I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda.
  \]
  The second equality follows by quotienting the Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis by the coordinate submodule defining \(I_{r,q}\).

## Strategy
Use source-2 lines 1310–1331; replace its parameter \(n-r\) by \(q\).
